chunks: And what he narrated - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father

: 'That Ali (peace be upon him) was brought a man who married a woman on top of her paternal aunt, so he lashed him and separated them.' There is nothing in these two narrations that contradicts what we have previously stated, because in the first narration it is not stated that it is not permissible for the man to combine between the woman and her paternal aunt and her maternal aunt with her consent or without consent, and likewise in the last narration which included that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) struck the one who married a woman on top of her maternal aunt, and if that was not in the apparent meaning of the narration and the first narration was detailed, then taking it is more preferable and acting upon it is more appropriate, and that which reveals what we mentioned and adds to its clarification is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does marrying a woman and her aunt simultaneously violate Islamic marriage laws according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *tarjih* (preference) by distinguishing between specific historical rulings and general legal prohibitions, arguing that the absence of explicit prohibition in the narrations allows for the permissibility of marrying both paternal and maternal aunts simultaneously. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on detailed evidence (*mufassal*) over general reports (*amm*) when deriving *ahkam* (legal rulings), highlighting the nuanced approach to *nikah* restrictions in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
